sections.h2: Which office bills and assesses property?
sections.html:
Tax Administration handles both sides of your bill. Rockingham County combines the assessor and collector jobs under one Tax Administrator, with an assessment division and a collection division. The office is in the Rockingham County Governmental Center, 371 NC Hwy 65, Reidsville, and is open weekdays. Call 336-342-8305 or write to PO Box 68, Wentworth, NC 27375, which is also the payment address.

The assessment division lists, appraises and assesses real property, business personal property and individual personal property. It also processes ownership transfers and keeps the records current. The collection division bills and collects current and delinquent taxes for the county, the City of Eden, the City of Reidsville, the Town of Madison, the Town of Mayodan, the Town of Stoneville and 18 rural fire districts. A house inside a town can therefore carry several levies.

Rates are set separately by the Board of County Commissioners, each fire district and each city or town council. They are established in June, and bills are mailed in late July.

sections.h2: Due dates and how to pay
sections.html:
Bills are due September 1 each year. You can pay with no interest through January 5, and the state rule starts interest on January 6.

After January 5 the state adds a flat two percent. From February 1 on it adds three-fourths of a percent for every month or part of a month. A prepayment discount exists only if the county or a town adopted one, so ask the collector about your current bill. A mailed payment counts on its postmark date.

Rockingham County accepts these payment methods:

  • A card payment online through the county's payment-service link, or an e-check through a second link
  • A call to 1-866-251-3264, with the bill in hand
  • A check mailed to Rockingham County Tax Collector, PO Box 68, Wentworth, NC 27375-0068
  • Counter service at the Governmental Center, which you should confirm with the office first

Since the budget sets the new rate in June and bills follow in late July, a spring listing still reflects last year's rate. Tell buyers to expect the figure to change.

You begin with an appraiser and, if needed, finish at the state Court of Appeals.

The informal step means calling the Real Property Division so an appraiser can recheck your record. It is open from January 1 until the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns. The Board is chosen by the county commissioners, is separate from the tax office staff, and starts hearing cases in April.

Rockingham County property value review levels
LevelWho decidesWhat to expect
1Real Property DivisionAppraiser review, January 1 through Board adjournment
2Board of Equalization and ReviewAppointed by the commissioners, hearings from April
3NC Property Tax CommissionFive members in Raleigh, hearings by application and appointment
4NC Court of AppealsLast resort for a dissatisfied owner

State statute requires the written request to arrive before the Board adjourns. An appeal to the Commission must follow within 30 days of the mailed decision. Between reappraisals, changes in value are limited by G.S. 105-287.

sections.h2: The 2024 reappraisal and what it means for you
sections.html:
Rockingham reappraised early because state sales ratio studies forced it. A ratio below 85% or above 115% requires a reappraisal within three years, and the county's ratios had fallen to 91.25% for 2020 sales, 77.86% for 2021 sales and 69.55% for 2022 sales. Tax values were far under market prices after the strong market that began in 2020.

Tax Administration worked with Piner Appraisal on the new values. The appraisers compared property cards with what they saw on site, tracked sales since the last reappraisal and studied rents and building costs. To value land, they grouped the county into about 500 zones called neighborhoods and set a land rate for each from local sales.

  • The new values took effect for 2024 tax bills and stay fixed until the next reappraisal, apart from changes the statutes allow.
  • Appeals for that cycle were heard in the spring of 2024, so a new appeal now needs a new notice of value.
  • A property card is available at the Tax Administration office in Wentworth or on the county website.

Here is a quick fairness test. When the assessed figure sits near the price you'd reasonably ask for the house, the appraisal is about right. Ask the office when the next reappraisal is scheduled.

Three state programs exist, and each owner may use just one. The county's Tax Forms page carries the 2026 Application for Property Tax Relief, the disability certification for the homestead exclusion and the certification for the disabled veteran exclusion. The same page lists a Present Use Value deferment application, a builder's exclusion and a Tax Certification Request form.

The homestead exclusion protects the larger of $25,000 or half the appraised value for older or disabled owners who stay under the $38,800 income limit printed on the 2026 state form. The disabled veteran exclusion takes off the first $45,000 regardless of age or income. The circuit breaker caps the bill at a share of income and defers the rest as a lien.

A deferral stays on the property. It comes due for the preceding three years if the owner sells, dies or stops living in the house, so a seller on that program should get a payoff early. For exemption questions, call the Tax Office at 336-342-8250.

Expect to cover your share of the current year's bill plus any earlier balance. The lien for a year's tax attaches to the parcel as of the January listing date, and interest and costs ride along with it. An overdue amount has to be cleared before a buyer gets clean title.

If a bill stays unpaid, the county can sue much as a lender would, and a courthouse auction may follow. Redeeming before the court confirms the sale means paying the tax plus penalties, interest and costs.

Before listing, ask the collection division for a payoff on every parcel number, fire district charges included. Your closing attorney then prorates the current year. When a house with back taxes sells fast, expect the title company to pay the balance from your proceeds at settlement.

A cash buyer can close without waiting on a lender's appraisal, but the tax lien still has to be paid or cleared at the table.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Rockingham County property taxes?
faqs.a: You pay the Rockingham County Tax Collector, online, by phone at 1-866-251-3264, or by mail to PO Box 68 in Wentworth. Keep your bill handy, since the phone option requires it.

faqs.q: Is the Tax Assessor a different office from the Tax Collector in Rockingham County?
faqs.a: No. Rockingham County combines the assessor and collector roles under one Tax Administrator, with an assessment division and a collection division inside the same office.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my value by phone?
faqs.a: Yes for the informal step. Call the Real Property Division and an appraiser will review the record and value. The formal step before the Board of Equalization and Review must be requested in writing on the county form.

faqs.q: What if I sell my Rockingham County house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: The lien follows the parcel, so the balance must be paid for title to pass cleanly. Your closing attorney normally pays it from your sale proceeds, so request a payoff amount from the collection division before closing.

faqs.q: Which towns send a tax bill collected by the county?
faqs.a: Besides the county bill, the collection division collects for the City of Eden, the City of Reidsville, the Town of Madison, the Town of Mayodan, the Town of Stoneville and 18 rural fire districts, so one parcel can carry several levies.
